questions.question: In story S12 (Join requests on the library inbox, auto-accept, pairing-ack split), is there any vacuous or placeholder production path: a no-op/stub body, a tautological assertion, a frozen stand-in constant, or an optional dependency (injected port, handler, client handle) that silently degrades to non-behavior when not injected? Cite file:line for each injection point in app/src/lib/marmot/joinRequestHandler.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/joinRequestSender.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/joinRequestStorage.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/outboundJoinRequests.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/joinRequestApproval.ts (new); app/src/lib/marmot/invitations/autoAccept.ts (new) and show that omitting the dependency fails loudly rather than succeeding silently.

Could `joinRequests` be deleted and rewritten without modifying any file outside its `dependencies_allowed` list? If not, which cross-module dependencies exist and do they flow through declared seam contracts in architecture.md (imports only via each module's index.ts, no React-context imports under app/src/lib/marmot/**, no ts-mls or @internet-privacy/marmot-ts imports)?

Does S12 comply with the architecture.md boundary rules: only `client/` constructs or disposes the MarmotClient, code inside HistoryBackend calls / inbox handlers / client listeners never awaits an account-scope client call (follow-up work via the owned setTimeout(0) FIFO), group sender identity comes only from orderingKey.account, and idb-keyval update() is not used? List each rule touched by this story's files with file:line evidence, or state why it is not touched.

Do unit, property, and (where the AC names them) library-harness or e2e tests cover the artifacts named in S12's scope (app/src/lib/marmot/joinRequestHandler.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/joinRequestSender.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/joinRequestStorage.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/outboundJoinRequests.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/joinRequestApproval.ts (new); app/src/lib/marmot/invitations/autoAccept.ts (new))? Show that tests use real collaborators or test fixtures rather than mocking the helper used at the SUT call site, that idb mocks are seeded out of key order where order matters, and that at least one test fails if the production code is replaced by a no-op.

Does the delivered S12 implementation match the intent of its scope (joinRequests: sendInboxRumor(21059) with send-failure state on retryable/failed, registerInboxHandler(21059) handler (rumor.pubkey, dedupe by rumor.id, deny layer, mute), approval via key-package lookup + single invite or no-op when a leaf exists, auto-accept correlation on inboxDisposition pending ) and respect its exclusions (MarmotContext wiring (S18); welcomeSubscription.ts deletion (S22))? Identify any capability owned by a later story that was built ahead, or any in-scope capability left unimplemented.

Which trust or validation boundaries does S12 touch (signer budget/permissions, relay-supplied events, rumor sender/pubkey attribution, invite/join payloads, privacy invariant that no profile metadata is published to public relays)? Show the validation or defensive check at each boundary with file:line evidence and a test that feeds a malformed or hostile input and observes rejection.

AC-JOIN-1: Join requests MUST be sent with `extensions.sendInboxRumor` of kind 21059; the join-request handler registered with `registerInboxHandler(21059)` MUST take the requester only from the delivered `rumor.pubkey`, dedupe by `rumor.id`, persist and return. Requester name/avatar travel inside the gift wrap only (recording transport: no kind 0, no cleartext nickname). Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [unit + harness] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

AC-JOIN-2: Approval MUST fetch the requester's key package (AC-KP-1/2) and call `group.invite` with exactly one event; the request is then marked approved. Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [unit + harness; e2e:groups-invite-link, groups-join-request-profile (kept)] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

AC-JOIN-3: Approving a requester whose account already holds a leaf in the group MUST issue no `group.invite` call, mark the request approved and consumed, and surface no error. Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [unit] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

AC-JOIN-4: A join-request send whose outcome is `retryable` or `failed` MUST put the request into the existing send-failure state; no retry timer is created by the app for it. Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [unit] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

AC-JOIN-5: Invite-link nonce, mute and dedup behaviour MUST be unchanged: replaying a join request with the same `rumor.id` or a muted requester MUST produce no new entry. Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [unit (existing join-request suite re-pointed); e2e:groups-invite-link (kept)] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

AC-AUTO-1: On `inboxDisposition: pending` with `groupId` and `sponsorAccount` matching an unexpired outbound join request, the app MUST call `invitations.accept(id)` exactly once (outside the listener frame, via the owned FIFO) and consume the request; a second matching event MUST NOT call accept. A non-matching invitation (different group, different sponsor, expired request) MUST stay pending with zero accept calls. The existing AC-AUTO rules apply unchanged. Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [unit + harness; e2e:groups-join-request-live (kept)] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

AC-AUTO-2: Auto-accept MUST have exactly one mechanism: no `keyPackages.offer` and no `expectWelcome` call exists in `app/src`. Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [structural] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies. Because the AC is structural, show the verification command's output on the pre-change tree and on the post-change tree and confirm they differ.

AC-INBOX-1: Pairing-ack (21060) MUST be handled by the existing NDK DM listener; that listener MUST silently skip kinds 444, 4460–4462, 21059 and 21064 (no error log, no state change). `welcomeSubscription.ts` MUST NOT exist. Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [unit; e2e:dm-pairing-* (kept)] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

AC-INBOX-2: Kind 21063 MUST NOT be sent or handled anywhere in `app/src` (only the retired-kind registry entry). Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [structural + AC-KIND-1] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies. Because the AC is structural, show the verification command's output on the pre-change tree and on the post-change tree and confirm they differ.
